items.titleZh: 拉塞尔美国站速度糟糕，与安东内利反差鲜明
items.summaryZh: 拉塞尔在美国大奖赛正赛仅列第八，落后夺冠的队友安东内利54秒，他将自己的速度形容为“糟糕透顶”。
items.originalTitle: The brutal Mercedes contrasts behind Russell's 'rubbish' pace
items.summaryEn: George Russell finished eighth at the United States Grand Prix, 54 seconds behind race winner and Mercedes team-mate Kimi Antonelli, describing his own pace as "rubbish".
detailZh: 困惑的乔治·拉塞尔对美国大奖赛上自己“糟糕”的速度找不到答案，这与志在夺冠的F1队友基米·安东内利形成了残酷反差。
拉塞尔最终第八完赛，落后分站冠军安东内利54秒；安东内利如今几乎已锁定在下周日墨西哥大奖赛加冕F1世界冠军。
安东内利本不太可能在奥斯汀就锁定冠军，但两位梅赛德斯车手之间的境遇差距如此之大，他差一点就提前做到了。
拉塞尔最终的差距和低迷名次，因五秒罚时的后果而被放大——这让他在比赛后半段被困在迈凯伦的奥斯卡·皮亚斯特里身后；但他对天空体育F1直言：“今天速度就是糟糕，这就是全部。
“那五秒大概让我丢了两三个位置。但在需要拿出速度的时候，速度不够好。”
拉塞尔尤其对糟糕的第一段 stint（ stint）感到警觉，这段表现甚至无法用陷入车流来合理解释，因为随着比赛推进，他落后伊萨克·哈贾尔的红牛赛车几秒钟。
这里本应有一些脏空气效应，但远不足以解释为什么拉塞尔平均每圈比安东内利慢零点八秒，并且越落越远，以至于早早采用两停策略的马克斯·维斯塔潘和夏尔·勒克莱尔都追上并重新超越了他，之后拉塞尔才终于进站。
拉塞尔称落后这么多很奇怪，随后不久他对包括 The Race 在内的媒体讲话时也没有答案，承认：“我需要给自己 24 小时来理清思路。”
第一段长距离 阶段是拉塞尔将整场比赛总结为“六圈好、五十圈糟”的重要原因。他第二次长距离使用硬胎的开局——在追上皮亚斯特里之前——是唯一相对亮点，但即便那时他也比安东内利每圈慢约零点一到零点二秒：更接近了，但仍然更慢，而且这是 stint 中可比较的部分，因为拉塞尔追皮亚斯特里时，安东内利也在追勒克莱尔。
“第一段 stint 节奏不好，但当我用硬胎出维修区后，大概有六圈我的圈速和基米一样，”拉塞尔说。“但后来我追上了奥斯卡，就是超不过去。”
皮亚斯特里的防守——以及/或者拉塞尔令人意外的难以发动进攻，仅在第37圈尝试一次便被挡回——确实毁了拉塞尔的比赛。他被困在皮亚斯特里的节奏里，迈凯伦让拉长的一停策略奏效，因此无法与安东内利的节奏直接比较。
不过拉塞尔的注意力在别处，因此强调：“我想弄明白为什么第一段 stint 节奏这么差。”但让困惑更深的是他补充道：“我需要和车队深入挖掘，因为当你落后这么多时，很难理解。”
目前所有的都只是理论。安东内利证明了升级后的梅赛德斯确实拥有出色的峰值表现，但拉塞尔可能正受困于人们谈论的那个狭窄的平衡窗口。
还有他们驾驶这些赛车和引擎的方式。拉塞尔和皮亚斯特里——领先车队中这一代赛车最挣扎的两位车手——本周末被队友碾压，这不可能只是巧合。
其中一部分原因一定在于他们在慢弯中操控赛车的舒适程度。在奥斯汀的排位赛中，拉塞尔在较快弯角能与安东内利匹敌，但在其他地方却持续落后。
安东内利显然更乐于应对车尾的滑动，并且在平衡推进程度而不让轮胎过度受力方面更为精准——但在奥斯汀，他总体上也更愿意牺牲一点入弯速度来最大化出弯表现。
如下方轨迹图所示，从12号弯到15号弯的损失被绘制出来，差值根据他们不同的入弯速度处理方式和出弯跑法而下降和上升，但最终安东内利在这一段结束时获得了决定性优势。
这也是安东内利相对于其他赛车特别强势的地方，而拉塞尔自从在这一段之前的11号弯出现一个小失误以来，就逐渐失去了对后轮温度的控制。
在排位赛中，拉塞尔在每个明显的慢速弯出弯处都比安东内利慢，而这些出弯处通常也通向主要的部署区域。
这里可能存在双重打击：安东内利在出弯和进入直道时携带更多速度，而且他在全油门方面的效率天生更高。而拉塞尔可能在不高效的油门区间花费更多时间。
梅赛德斯车队老板托托·沃尔夫推测，拉塞尔在梅赛德斯以领先姿态开启周末时表现最强，但当车队发现情况更艰难时，他受到的困扰更大——如果升级的特性会放大这种不适，这可能是第一个真实的例子。
“当我们将赛车调整到适合他的方式时，他绝对很快，”沃尔夫说。“但当它掉出那个工作窗口时，他就会挣扎。而且他比基米可能挣扎得更多。这是我们的责任。
“我们只需要和他一起弄清楚，为什么驾驶表现会有这么大的差异，因为乔治并不是比基米慢半秒、慢十分之三秒。绝对根本不是这种情况。
“那么他不喜欢的是什么？我们需要在改装赛车、以不同方式设置赛车让他跑快方面做些什么？”
在赛季已经深入到这个阶段还在问这些问题，考虑到拉塞尔近期的进步，这并不理想——他此前似乎在逐步缩小赛季中期对安东内利出现的最严重劣势。
但也值得强调，安东内利在奥斯汀表现极为出色，因此给拉塞尔形成了格外鲜明的反差。尽管外界对拉塞尔的状态百思不得其解，沃尔夫也承认，梅赛德斯本赛季同样没有预料到安东内利会有如此大的进步，而这正是他成长为一名高质量车手的最新例证。
安东内利在排位赛中表现出色，在赛车最强的环节充分压榨出圈速，也就是第一赛段的中高速连续弯，并且出色地控制后轮打滑，弥补了赛车整个周末在低速12、13和15号弯最薄弱的环节。
而在正赛中，得益于身后赛车互相缠斗、早早给他带来两秒的缓冲，他通过保持稳定优势，立刻化解了使用软胎的对手对他中性胎可能构成的任何威胁。
随后他毫无波澜地完成了一次进站策略，尽管对硬胎并不熟悉，而且策略是在第一段 stint 后于比赛中期才锁定的。甚至他在赛道限制上频繁试探的倾向，在关键时刻也完全得到了控制。
“在基米这边，主要的头条是，对我来说，这是他迄今为止奉献的最棒的一场比赛，”沃尔夫说道。“这是一场尚未成为冠军的冠军所展现的比赛，但非常出色。”
在一个标准极高的赛季中，这是一个大胆的论断——其中包括在摩纳哥的惊艳表现，以及最著名的，安东内利在蒙扎从第19位发车夺冠。或许安东内利最令人印象深刻的是他完成这一切的轻松自如。
没有锁定冠军的压力，因为一段时间以来这实际上已是板上钉钉的事，但即便经历了本赛季最大的失误——在阿塞拜疆排位赛中撞车——以及梅赛德斯随后在赛车升级上的波动，他依然毫不松懈。
这是两位车手之间形成鲜明对比的又一个例子。拉塞尔在顺境中拼得更凶，在逆境中则更容易、也更戏剧性地陷入低谷。对安东内利来说，这一切都如此自然，显得毫不费力，让他能够反复攀上新的高度——因此他认为，就自己和车队所做的工作而言，这一站的表现超过了蒙扎。
“蒙扎，我们显然拥有最快的赛车，”安东内利说。“我们就是超级快，所以从后面追上来当然非常特别，但那也是一条相对容易超车的赛道，而且我们那么快。
“毫无疑问，蒙扎是非常特别的一站，也是我会永远记住的一站。但这一站，就执行层面而言，可能更好，因为我们逐步积累、在整个周末逐步提升表现的方式非常出色。”
detailEn: A confused George Russell lacked answers for his “rubbish” pace at the United States Grand Prix, which contrasted brutally with his championship-bound Formula 1 team-mate Kimi Antonelli.
Russell finished eighth and 54 seconds behind race winner Antonelli, who is now all but guaranteed to become F1 world champion in next Sunday’s Mexican Grand Prix.
It was unlikely that Antonelli would seal the deal in Austin but such was the difference in fortunes between the Mercedes drivers he very nearly pulled it off.

Russell’s final margin and his lowly position was exaggerated by the consequences of a five-second penalty that meant he got stuck behind McLaren’s Oscar Piastri in the second half of the race, but as he bluntly told Sky Sports F1: “The pace was just rubbish today, that’s the long and short of it.
“The five seconds probably cost me two or three positions. But the pace was not good enough when it needed to be.”

Russell was particularly alarmed by a poor opening stint that cannot even be explained satisfactorily by being in traffic, because he slipped back a few seconds behind Isack Hadjar’s Red Bull as it progressed.

There would have been some dirty air effect here, but not nearly enough to explain why Russell was eight tenths a lap slower than Antonelli on average and drifted so far away that early two-stoppers Max Verstappen and Charles Leclerc had caught and re-passed him before Russell finally came in.
Russell called it strange to be so far off, and when he spoke to media including The Race shortly afterwards he had no answers, admitting: “I need to give myself 24 hours to think clearly”.

That first stint is a large part of why Russell summed his race up as “six good laps, 50 bad laps”. The start of his second long stint on hards - before catching Piastri - the only relative bright spot, but even then he seemed around a tenth or two slower than Antonelli: closer, but still slower, and this is a comparable part of the stint because while Russell was catching Piastri, Antonelli was catching Leclerc.

“The pace wasn't good on the first stint, but when I came out of pits on the hard, I probably did six laps where I was lapping the same pace as Kimi,” Russell said. “But then I caught Oscar and I just couldn't overtake.”

Piastri’s defence - and/or Russell’s surprising difficulty in making a move, with only a single attempt on lap 37 rebuffed - did indeed kill Russell’s race. He was stuck at Piastri’s pace as McLaren made a stretched one-stop work, and so a direct comparison with Antonelli’s pace was not possible.

Russell’s focus was elsewhere, though, hence stressing: “I want to understand why the pace was so bad on the first stint”. But to compound the confusion he added: “I need to dig deep with my team because it's difficult to understand when you're so far off.”
All there are, for now, are theories. Antonelli proved that the upgraded Mercedes does have a wonderful peak, but Russell may be suffering from the narrow balance window that has been talked about.

There’s also the way they simply drive these cars and engines. It cannot be a coincidence that Russell and Piastri, the two chief strugglers of this generation of car among the leading teams, received a pasting from their team-mates this weekend.

Some of that must be in how comfortable they are manipulating the car in slow corners. Russell was there with Antonelli in the faster turns in qualifying at Austin, but consistently losing out elsewhere.

Antonelli definitely seems happier living with the rear moving around and is more precise in balancing how much to push that without over-stressing the tyres – but in Austin he was also, generally, willing to sacrifice a little bit of corner entry speed to maximise his exit.

As the below trace shows, charting the loss from Turn 12 to 15, the delta falls and rises based on their different entry speed approaches and runs off the corner, but it culminates in Antonelli eventually having a decisive advantage by the end of the sequence.

This is where Antonelli was particularly strong versus other cars too, whereas Russell has gradually lost control of rear tyre temperature ever since a small error way back before this sequence at Turn 11.
Russell was slower than Antonelli on every prominent slower corner exit in qualifying, and these usually lead into the main deployment zones too.

There could be a double whammy here, with Antonelli carrying more speed off the corner and onto the straight, but also being inherently more efficient in how he is often sharper onto full throttle. Whereas Russell potentially spends more time in an inefficient throttle range.

Mercedes team boss Toto Wolff theorised that Russell has been strongest when Mercedes has started weekends on the front foot but suffered more when it has found things tougher - if the upgrade’s characteristics can exaggerate that discomfort, this could have been the first real example of it.

“When we land the car in the way that suits him, he's absolutely fast,” said Wolff. “But when it drops out of that operating window, he struggles. And he struggles more than maybe Kimi. And that is on us.

“ We just have to work it out with him how there can be such a difference in driving in performance because George is not half a second slower, three tenths slower than Kimi. It's just absolutely not the case.
“So what is it that he doesn't like? What is it that we need to do in terms of modifying the car, setting it up in a different way for him to go fast?”

That these questions are still being asked deep into the season is not great given the recent progress Russell seemed to have made, chipping away at the worst of his deficit to Antonelli that emerged through the middle of the season.

But it’s also worth stressing that Antonelli was magnificent at Austin, and therefore presented Russell with an especially harsh contrast. For all of the head-scratching over Russell’s form, Wolff has admitted that Mercedes didn’t see such a big step from Antonelli this season coming either, with this being the latest example of what a high-quality driver he has evolved into.

Antonelli excelled in qualifying to wring the neck out of the car in its strongest parts around the lap, namely the medium and high speed Esses in the opening sector, and control the rear tyre slip excellently to mitigate where it had been weakest all weekend in the slow-speed Turns 12, 13 and 15.

And in the race, aided by cars squabbling behind and giving him a two-second buffer early on, he immediately neutralised any threat he might have faced from those on softs to his mediums by maintaining a steady advantage.

Then he executed a one-stop without any hint of fuss, despite unfamiliarity with the hard tyre and the strategy being locked in mid-race after the first stint. Even his tendency to flirt extensively with track limits seemed totally under control when it counted.
“On Kimi's side, the main headline is that, for me, the best race that he's delivered so far,” Wolff said. “The race of a champion who isn't the champion yet, but exceptional.”

That is a big claim in a season of extremely high standards that includes a tremendous showing in Monaco and, most famously, Antonelli’s win from 19th on the grid at Monza. Perhaps what was most impressive about Antonelli was the ease with which he produced this.

There is no pressure to secure the title, because it has been effectively a foregone conclusion for a while, but he has been relentless even through his biggest mistake of the season - crashing in qualifying in Azerbaijan - and Mercedes’ subsequent wobble with its car upgrade.

That is another example of the contrast between the two drivers. Russell’s fighting harder for the good moments and falls into the bad ones more easily and dramatically. For Antonelli, this is all so natural, and comes across as effortless, allowing him to repeatedly scale new heights - hence his agreement this topped Monza in terms of the job he and the team did.

“Monza, we clearly had the fastest car,” said Antonelli. “We were just super quick, so of course it was incredibly special coming from the back, but it was also a track where it was relatively easy to overtake, and we were so quick.

“Definitely, Monza was a super special one, and one that I will remember forever. But, this one probably, in terms of execution, was better, because the way we built up and the way we built the performance throughout the weekend was very good.”

拉塞尔对天空体育F1表示，五秒罚时大概让他损失了两到三个位置，但速度在需要时不够好。

detailZh: 乔治·拉塞尔的梅赛德斯F1未来在基米·安东内利成功后受到质疑
詹姆斯·欣克利夫建议乔治·拉塞尔可以考虑离开梅赛德斯
对于梅赛德斯车迷来说，这里是关于银箭的最新消息，包括F1新闻、车手更新、赛车发展和比赛分析，来自布拉克利和布里克斯沃斯。
乔治·拉塞尔在美国大奖赛之后，他的梅赛德斯F1长期未来受到质疑
拉塞尔作为夺冠热门之一进入了2026赛季的F1，但在赢得赛季揭幕战澳大利亚大奖赛和中国短道赛之后，这位英国车手眼睁睁地看着他的队友基米·安东内利成为了最年轻的世界冠军车手。
在赢得美国大奖赛后，安东内利以365分的积分领跑积分榜，而拉塞尔以242分位居第二。这位意大利车手在美洲赛道上错失了夺冠的机会，但在墨西哥大奖赛上还有机会。
在F1 Nation播客上，F1电视评论员、前IndyCar车手詹姆斯·辛克莱夫讨论了拉塞尔未来可能考虑离开Brackley车队的选择。
‘这是一个非常独特的情况，因为基米是托托[沃尔夫]亲自挑选的，一路从青训车队成长起来的，’辛克莱夫解释道。
“他是梅赛德斯的作品。他是托托的作品。而乔治，虽然程度稍低，也是梅赛德斯家族的一员。显然，他在威廉姆斯车队，被培养来接替刘易斯。这一年，他必须真正确立自己的权威。”
“你永远不会把一年看作是作为车手被队友击败，然后想，‘哦，我完了。这个人比我强。’你会想，‘他今年比我强，但我可以反弹回来。我仍然可以让自己成为这个团队的一部分。’
“但当你考虑所有因素，他做到的方式，他的年轻，他在职业生涯中这么早做到这一点，他是托托的个人项目。即使你不是那个人，至少你大脑的1%也至少有过这样的想法[考虑其他可能性]。”
他补充说：“这里的关键是，乔治的合同去年花了很长时间才被签署、宣布，等等。那些对话已经开始了，对吧？所以尽管很明显他会回到那里，我知道他的管理层已经走遍了赛道，并与人们进行了交谈。”
“所以那些关系已经建立。关于‘26年的那些对话最初是开启的。没有什么可以说那些对话不能很快重新开始。”
detailEn: George Russell's Mercedes F1 future discussed amid Kimi Antonelli's success
James Hinchcliffe has suggested George Russell could consider leaving Mercedes
For Mercedes fans. All the latest from the Silver Arrows, with F1 news, driver updates, car development and race analysis from Brackley and Brixworth.
George Russell's long-term future at Mercedes has been questioned following the United States Grand Prix.

Russell entered the 2026 Formula 1 season as one of the favourites for the title. But after winning the season-opening Australian Grand Prix and the Chinese sprint race, the Briton watched as his team-mate Kimi Antonelli became the youngest driver to lead the championship.

After winning the United States Grand Prix in Austin, Antonelli now leads the standings with 365 points, and Russell sits second with 242 points. The Italian driver missed out on claiming the championship at the Circuit of the Americas, but has another chance at the Mexican Grand Prix.
Speaking on the F1 Nation podcast, F1 TV pundit and former IndyCar driver James Hinchcliffe discussed the possibility of Russell considering his options away from the Brackley outfit in the future.
"It's such a unique situation because Kimi was handpicked by Toto [Wolff], brought up through the ladder," Hinchcliffe explained.

"He is a Mercedes creation. He's a Toto creation. And you've got George, who was similar to a lesser extent, was part of the Mercedes family. They had him at Williams, obviously, being groomed to take over for Lewis. And this was kind of the year that he had to really stamp that authority.

"You're never going to look at one year as a driver getting beat by your team-mate and think, 'Oh, I'm washed. This guy's better than me.' You're going to think, 'He was better than me this year, but I can bounce back. I can still make this team my own.'

"But when you look at all the factors, the way in which he's done it, how young he is, how early he did it in his career, the fact that he was Toto's personal project. Even if you're not that guy, 1% of your brain at minimum has to at least have had that thought [of potentially looking elsewhere]."

He added: "Here's the thing. George's contract took a while to get picked up, announced, whatever, last year. Those conversations already started, right? So even though it was pretty obvious he was going to end up back there, I know for a fact that his management went up and down the paddock and had conversations with people.
"So those relationships have already been established. Those conversations were opened about '26 originally. There's nothing to say that those conversations can't be struck back up pretty quickly."

detailZh: 迈凯伦为何在美国大奖赛向奥斯卡·皮亚斯特里下达车队指令
奥斯卡·皮亚斯特里在奥斯汀比赛早期让兰多·诺里斯通过，安德烈亚·斯特拉说明这完全合理
迈凯伦车队领队安德烈亚·斯特拉解释了在美国大奖赛要求奥斯卡·皮亚斯特里让兰多·诺里斯超越的原因。
皮亚斯特里和诺里斯在美洲赛道排位赛第三节未能挑战梅赛德斯、红牛和法拉利，最终占据第四排发车位。
然而，在比赛的前七圈中，皮亚斯特里每圈比领跑者安东内利慢一秒——除去第一圈，平均恰好慢0.997秒——甚至跟不上苦苦挣扎的拉塞尔，后者每圈还能拉开零点二秒。
诺里斯在无线电中抱怨被队友“挡住”；迈凯伦要求这位澳大利亚车手让队友通过，他在第八圈一号弯照做了。诺里斯随后在七圈内拉开了四秒。
“我们在周末期间看到，兰多比奥斯卡稍快一些，”斯特拉详细说道。“这是一条兰多擅长的赛道，也是奥斯卡相对更吃力一些的赛道之一。
兰多·诺里斯，迈凯伦，奥斯卡·皮亚斯特里，迈凯伦，安德烈亚·斯特拉，迈凯伦
“今年对奥斯卡来说尤其棘手，因为奥斯卡的超能力是逐步建立参照；一旦他建立起参照，他就能真正高效地一圈接一圈地跑。但在这里每一圈都不同，所以这些条件对奥斯卡构成了挑战，实际上也正是兰多发挥自己超能力的条件——那就是对条件极强的适应能力，尤其是在赛车打滑的时候。”
“所以，鉴于这种情况，我们在赛前讨论过，如果兰多跟在奥斯卡后面，而奥斯卡跟不上前面的赛车，那我们就可以给兰多一个机会或可能性，看看我们能否向前面的赛车发起攻击——我们就是这么做的。”
这对迈凯伦意义重大，此前其车手在新加坡冲刺赛中相撞。“这是一种展示，表明作为一支车队，并且与车手们一起，我们关心车队的利益，这一直是我们之间的对话，”斯特拉补充道。
“尤其是在新加坡之后，我们进一步强调了大家齐心协力帮助迈凯伦回到我们想要的位置有多么重要，那就是奥斯卡和兰多在排位赛中占据头排，为胜利而战，然后我们再管理内部竞争。但在此之前，大家必须齐心协力，维持迈凯伦重返前列的轨迹。”
迈凯伦在周日选择了进站一次的策略，试图挑战其他顶尖车队，而法拉利双雄刘易斯·汉密尔顿和查尔斯·勒克莱尔，以及马克斯·维斯塔潘则采用进站两次的策略。诺里斯因此一直保持第二名直到第46圈，随后被这三位车手超越——但他在升至第五名的过程中仍然成功对伊萨克·哈贾尔和拉塞尔实施了提前进站，皮亚斯特里同样击败了银箭车队车手升至第七。
“我们尝试使用硬胎，这在练习中似乎很有竞争力，而且我们知道其他车队会使用更软配方的轮胎，”斯特拉解释道。“当我们看到第一阶段（stint）的情况，以及他们有些挣扎的事实时，我们得到了一些鼓励，认为使用硬胎可能是追赶的好方法。
“所以，在第二阶段我们实际上相比两辆法拉利和维斯塔潘在追赶。在某个阶段，我们决定采用进站一次的策略，因为如果进站两次，我们总会落在后面。进站一次让你有可能利用安全车的机会，但安全车没有出现。我们仍在等待对马德里发生事情的补偿——它会来的，”这位意大利人补充道，指的是诺里斯在马德里赛道因不合时宜的虚拟安全车时段而失去了潜在的胜利。
“我们也尝试看看硬胎还剩多少性能，但老实说，我们知道我们极不可能将维斯塔潘，尤其是勒克莱尔挡在身后。对于汉密尔顿，我们认为这更多取决于硬胎最后阶段的表现。没人能预知，但值得一试。”
“我们对策略执行感到满意；我们对今天基本弄清了该用哪些轮胎感到满意；对赛车似乎因升级而有所提升感到满意。但我们需要提升排位赛表现，而且如果想持续争夺领奖台、尤其是争夺胜利，我们还需要继续改进赛车。”
迈凯伦已连续四轮无缘领奖台，按这一指标衡量，这是自2023赛季最后两轮以及2024夺冠赛季前两轮以来，他们最差的一段状态。
detailEn: Why McLaren gave team order to Oscar Piastri in F1 US GP
Oscar Piastri let Lando Norris through early on in Austin, and it made perfect sense, Andrea Stella demonstrates
McLaren team principal Andrea Stella has explained the reasoning behind asking Oscar Piastri to wave Lando Norris past in Formula 1’s United States Grand Prix.
Piastri and Norris locked out the fourth row of the grid at the Circuit of The Americas, having failed to challenge the Mercedes, Red Bulls and Ferraris in Q3.

However, over the first seven laps of the race, Piastri lost one second per lap to race leader Kimi Antonelli – precisely 0.997s on average, discounting lap one – and couldn’t even keep up with a struggling George Russell, who was pulling away by two tenths a lap.

Norris complained on the radio he was “being held up” by his team-mate; McLaren asked the Australian to let his team-mate through, which he duly did in Turn 1 on lap eight. Norris went on to pull away by four seconds in seven laps.

“We had seen during the weekend that Lando was a little bit faster than Oscar,” Stella detailed. “This is a track in which Lando excels and is one of the tracks in which Oscar instead struggles a little bit more.
Lando Norris, McLaren, Oscar Piastri, McLaren, Andrea Stella, McLaren

“This year, in particular for Oscar, is tricky because Oscar's superpower is to build; once he creates references, he can really effectively build lap after lap. But here every lap is different, so these are the conditions that challenge Oscar and actually are the conditions where Lando uses his own superpower, which is being very adaptive to the conditions, especially as the car slides.

“So, given this context, we discussed before the race that if Lando was behind Oscar, and Oscar could not keep up with the cars ahead, then we could have given Lando a chance or an opportunity to see if we could attack the cars ahead – and that's what we did.”

This meant a lot to McLaren after its drivers collided in the Singapore sprint race. “It's a way of demonstrating that as a team and together with the drivers, we care about the interests of the team, which was always the conversation that we have had,” Stella added.

“And especially after Singapore, we reinforced how much it's important that we all together help McLaren go back to the position that we want to have, which is Oscar and Lando, first row in qualifying, fighting for the win, and then we manage the internal competition. But up to then, all together, we need to sustain the trajectory of McLaren back to the front.”

McLaren picked a one-stop strategy in a bid to challenge the other top teams on Sunday, with Ferrari duo Lewis Hamilton and Charles Leclerc, plus Max Verstappen on two stops. Norris consequently held second place until lap 46, before succumbing to those three drivers – but he still managed to undercut Isack Hadjar and Russell on his way to fifth place, with Piastri likewise beating the Silver Arrow to seventh.

“We tried to deploy the hard tyres, which in practice seemed to be competitive, and we knew that the others were going for the softer side of the tyre allocation,” Stella explained. “Once we saw the first stint and the fact that they were struggling a bit, we got some encouragement that using the hard tyres could have been a good way of catching up.

“So, we were actually catching up compared to the two Ferraris and Verstappen in the second stint. At some stage, we just decided to go for the one-stop, because if we go for a two, we are always going to stay behind. The one-stop gives you the possibility to take advantage of a safety car, which didn't come. We are still waiting for a compensation for what happened in Madrid – it will come,” the Italian added, referring to Norris losing a potential win to an untimely VSC period at Madring.

“We also attempted to see what's left in the hard tyres, but honestly, we knew that it was very, very unlikely that we could have kept Verstappen and in particular Leclerc behind. With Hamilton, we thought it was more dependent on the final tail of the hard tyres. Nobody could have known, but worthwhile giving it a go.

“We are happy with the strategy execution; we are happy with the fact that we kind of understood which tyres needed to be used today; happy with the fact that the car seems to have improved thanks to the upgrades. But we need to improve our qualifying performance, and we also need to keep improving the car if we want to consistently compete for podiums, but above all for victories.”
McLaren is on a four-round podiumless streak, its worst spell of form by that metric since the last two rounds of the 2023 season and the first two of its title-winning 2024 campaign.

items.originalTitle: Edd Straw's 2026 United States Grand Prix F1 driver rankings
detailZh: 从美国大奖赛周末开始，F1车手排名采用新的层级列表格式（从Tier S到Tier F），而非之前的1-22排名。
每个层级除了一个外，都限制为五名车手，Tier S仅适合一个名字，这次的选择并不复杂。
通常，你可以在The Race Members' Club的帖子下评论提问关于Edd的排名，并尝试使用我们方便的视觉工具编制自己的美国大奖赛层级列表！
你可以在文章底部阅读Edd关于格式变化的完整理由。
尽管车队负责人托托·沃尔夫声称这是基米·安东内利的最佳比赛可能有些言过其实，但安东内利无疑是这场赛事的亮点。
他不仅在速度上明显优于队友乔治·拉塞尔，而且在Q3的第一轮练习中就锁定了杆位，尽管起步时处于中胎的劣势，但他仍然取得了良好的起步。这一切，加上选择单停策略，是他在一场本可能因为红牛和法拉利的速度而变得复杂的比赛中相对顺利获胜的关键。
这种舒适的领先位置是安东内利出色执行的结果。
利亚姆·劳森的周末大部分时间都表现得无懈可击，在中场战中占据主导地位。唯一的缺点是在Q2中被小红牛队友阿维德·林德布拉德以0.108秒的差距超越 - 但考虑到车队为了最小化林德布拉德发车线处罚的影响而决定不让他参加Q3，这也很难过多指责他。
同样，皮埃尔·加斯利尽管从未完全适应阿尔卑斯赛车，但仍然在很大程度上最大化了其性能。他在最后的Q2练习中找到了速度，将赛车提升到第11快的成绩，然后在发车时一度领先劳森，但在第1弯道又落后于他。在奥利·贝尔曼的碰撞后，他右侧面板受损，但尽管如此，他还是坚持到了积分赛结束。
查尔斯·勒克莱尔在整个比赛中都是法拉利的更快车手，并驾驶着一辆强劲的赛车，在两停策略下获得了第二名。唯一的负面因素是Q3练习中有些吃力，尽管这在很大程度上是由于当时法拉利在那里的特性。
费尔南多·阿隆索是唯一三名在复杂的排位赛中连续刷新个人最佳成绩的车手之一，并且他认为自己在比赛中有机会获得积分。但相反，他不得不与第一圈在发夹弯被亚历克斯·阿隆索撞击造成的损坏作斗争。
马克斯·维斯塔潘在排位赛中稍微有点后轮抓地力问题，差点被队友伊萨克·哈吉亚超越，在一场最终以0.036秒的优势获胜的面对面较量中。尽管策略并不理想，他还是设法获得了第三名，尽管虚拟安全车阻碍了刘易斯·汉密尔顿的进攻。
汉密尔顿虽然设置得没有勒克莱尔那么好，但他的预赛劣势很小。他在整个周末都取得了良好的进步，如果不是因为虚拟安全车（VSC），他可能已经获得了第三名。
在新加坡周末的困难之后，哈德贾做出了强劲的恢复。他几乎超过了维斯塔潘的预赛成绩，并且很好地处理了他在比赛中的问题，即使他的无线电信息并没有表现出这一点。在那种情况下，他得到了一个相当不错的成绩。
尼克·胡肯伯格将奥迪赛车大致放在了应该在的位置，即预赛和比赛中都位于前十之外。然而，如果预赛执行得完美，可能还能在奥迪赛车中得分，这一事实让他稳居排名中间位置。
尽管在周末的大部分时间里处于劣势，林德布拉德还是出色地完成了工作，从Q3中拉出了一个位置，尽管五位的网格处罚让他付出了代价，他从未能够进入严重的积分争夺。
塞尔吉奥·佩雷斯在凯迪拉克车手之间略快一些，但在排位赛中并没有完全发挥出车辆的全部潜力。他在软胎起步后并没有轻松地完成比赛，这意味着他比预期的更早陷入了蓝旗噩梦。
兰多·诺里斯很快，但据他自己承认，他在Q3中表现不佳，最终落后于他的速度较慢的队友。他的比赛驾驶执行得很好，但他的结果潜力从根本上受到了周六发生的事情的限制。
加布里埃尔·博尔特洛托看起来像是奥迪车手中速度更快的那位，但网格处罚意味着他无法正常攻击排位赛——尽管在Q1中获得第六名已经树立了标志。他的比赛表现不错，但让他失去更高一级别位置的是，他在VSC部署时错误地进入维修区，这意味着他最终排名第13，而不是第12。
奥斯卡·皮亚斯蒂在速度上从未达到队友诺里斯的水平。让他避免掉到更低一级别的因素是他能够在大比例的比赛中保持领先于拉塞尔。
卡洛斯·塞恩斯在威廉姆斯车队的表现总体上很稳健。然而，尽管他将责任归咎于林德布拉德挤压他进入维修区墙壁，但将他的威廉姆斯车试图塞入如此小的间隙是一个高风险的决定——因此他必须为结果承担一些责任。
在两辆凯迪拉克中，瓦尔特里·博塔斯稍微慢一些，但差距并不大。在被迫退赛之前，他本应大致完成他应该完成的比赛。
埃斯特班·奥康的周末受到了车辆问题的困扰，这使得很难评估他接近车辆极限的程度。但在他习惯性的强劲起步之后，他在这种情况下驾驶了一场不错的比赛。
这一级别包括的车手们，在不同程度上缺乏他们队友的速度，在两起事故中，这种情况进一步加剧。
拉塞尔从未关注过队友安东内利的水平，加上第一圈的超车线违规，即使处罚可能有些严厉，这也导致他被判罚到顶级四队组的最后一名。
拉塞尔与安东内利的差距与斯特罗尔与阿隆索的差距相似，这使得他的#18号阿斯顿·马丁车队成为后位车队，而不是像#14号那样的中场竞争者。即使是维修区起步也是部分原因，需要处理受损部件。
奥利·比尔曼的周末大部分时间都让他有资格进入高等级别，但他并没有在排位赛中充分利用自己的速度，因为他的最终Q2圈被删除，排名从第13位降至第16位，尽管他强烈反对。在13号弯与加斯利的碰撞给他造成了损害，毁了大奖赛，尽管他抗议，但 stewards 仍然认为他负有责任。
在威廉姆斯车队中，在结果方面几乎不可能取得任何成绩，但亚历克斯·阿隆·邦的排位赛表现一般，比萨因斯慢了两十分。虽然他在第一圈发夹弯与阿隆索的碰撞远非阿隆索所说的那样严重，但这确实是一次高风险的动作，给阿隆·邦造成了翼片损坏，这影响了他的比赛。
科拉平托因为自己没有错而被10个位置的网格处罚，这意味着他对加斯利的资格赛劣势并不是他排名的主要原因——因为他整个周末都没有专注于低油量速度练习。然而，他的整体速度从未产生影响，在1号弯撞上Lindblad是一个错误，最终导致他退出了比赛。
有三个明显的原因。第一个是最重要的，因为它是一种更准确的方式，在比赛周末的速度、一致性、赛车技巧、错误以及与车手技艺相关的无数其他标准上比较车手的性能。
通常，反馈会关注为什么两个处于同一水平但排名不同的车手之间可能会有5个位置的差距，而等级列表允许他们平等排名，同时保持他们相对于其他车手的位置。通过将车手分组，并提供七个可用等级，这是一种更有意义的方式来区分不同水平上表现的车手群体。
第二个原因是，这也更容易理解我们认为哪些车手做得比其他人更好或更差。通过消除需要无限小的差异，这应该会使这项练习更具揭示性。反馈通常关注为什么，例如，在排名中间，两个队友之间可能会有4个位置的差距，而他们的表现之间几乎没有或没有有意义的不同。等级列表避免了这种情况，并允许关注更明显的差异。
第三点是，这是一种更现代、更直观的方式来展示运动员的表现比较。我们团队制作出的出色图形比任何文字都能更有效地证明这一点。
在排名上，我们仍然会投入同样的严谨和努力，但《The Race》认为，这是我们提供分析水平的一种更现代、更具代表性的方式。
detailEn: A new Formula 1 driver rankings format is here starting from the United States Grand Prix weekend - with a tier list version (from Tier S to Tier F) instead of the 1-22 ranking.
Every tier but one is limited to five drivers, with Tier S fit for just one name - and it wasn't a particularly complicated choice to make this time.
As usual, you can ask your questions about Edd's rankings by commenting on this post in The Race Members' Club - and have a crack at compiling your own US GP tier list with our handy visual tool!
You can read Edd's full reasoning as to the change in format at the bottom of the article.
Although team principal Toto Wolff's claim this was Kimi Antonelli's best race was perhaps a touch overstated, Antonelli was the standout choice.

Not only did he have a clear pace advantage over team-mate George Russell, but he also nailed it on the first run of Q3 to seal pole, then made a good start despite the disadvantage of mediums. That, and the choice to one-stop, was key to a relatively straightforward victory in a race that could have been far more complicated given the pace of Red Bull and Ferrari.
That comfortable position was the consequence of Antonelli's outstanding execution.

Liam Lawson's weekend was one of largely unobtrusive excellence, dominating the midfield battle. The only caveat was that he was outpaced by Racing Bulls team-mate Arvid Lindblad in Q2 by 0.108s - but it's difficult to hold this against him too much given the team's decision not to run him in Q3 to minimise the impact of Lindblad's grid penalty.

Similarly, Pierre Gasly largely maximised the Alpine despite never being entirely comfortable with the car. He found pace on his final Q2 run to put the car 11th-fastest, then after momentarily getting ahead of Lawson at the start slipped behind him at Turn 1. He carried floor damage on the right side after the Ollie Bearman collision but despite that held on to a points finish.

Charles Leclerc was the quicker Ferrari driver throughout and drove a strong race to take second place on the two-stopper. The only negative was that Q3 was a struggle, although as much as anything that was down to the characteristics of the Ferrari in those conditions.

Fernando Alonso was one of only three drivers to string together his three personal-best sectors in a tricky qualifying session - and felt he had a shot at points in the race. But instead he had to battle damage sustained when he was hit by Alex Albon at the hairpin on the first lap.

Max Verstappen struggled a little for rear grip in qualifying and was close to being outqualified by team-mate Isack Hadjar, in a head-to-head battle he ultimately won by just 0.036s. But despite the strategy not being ideal he managed to take third place, albeit with the virtual safety car hindering Lewis Hamilton's charge.

Hamilton didn't nail the set-up quite as well as Leclerc, though his qualifying deficit to his team-mate was small. He made good progress throughout the weekend and probably would have finished third without the VSC.

This was a strong recovery from Hadjar after a difficult Singapore weekend. He almost outqualified Verstappen and dealt well with his in-race problems, even if his radio messages didn't suggest that was the case. He banked a decent result in the circumstances.

Nico Hulkenberg put the Audi broadly where it should have been, just outside the top 10 in both qualifying and the race. However, with a perfectly executed qualifying it was probably possible to score in the Audi - this fact putting him firmly in the middle of the pack of the rankings.

Having been on the back foot for much of the weekend, Lindblad did a good job to pull a Q3 place out of the bag, although the five-place grid penalty cost him and he was never able to get himself into serious points contention.

Sergio Perez was marginally the faster of the Cadillac drivers but didn't get everything out of the car in qualifying. He didn't have the easiest race after starting on softs, meaning he ended up being stuck in a blue-flag nightmare earlier than he'd have liked.

Lando Norris was quick, but by his own admission he did a bad job in Q3 and ended up behind his much slower team-mate. His race drive was well-executed, but his result potential was fundamentally limited by what happened on Saturday.

Gabriel Bortoleto appeared to be the Audi driver with that extra edge of pace but the grid penalties meant he wasn't able to attack qualifying properly - although sixth in Q1 did lay down a marker. His race was good, but what costs him a place in a higher tier was mistakenly bringing himself into the pits when the VSC was deployed, meaning he finished 13th rather than 12th.
Oscar Piastri never looked at team-mate Norris's level in terms of his pace. What saves him from being a tier lower is that he was able to keep Russell behind for a large proportion of the race.

Carlos Sainz was largely solid in the Williams. However, while he blamed Lindblad for squeezing him into the pitwall, it was a high-risk decision to try to put his Williams into such a small gap - so he has to bear some responsibility for the outcome.
Of the two Cadillacs, Valtteri Bottas was marginally the slower but it wasn't by much. He was on course to finish broadly where he should have done before being forced to retire late.

Esteban Ocon's weekend was compromised by car problems, making it difficult to evaluate how close he got to the maximum of the car. But he drove a decent race in the circumstances after his customary strong start.
This tier comprises drivers who, to varying degrees, lacked the pace of their team-mates, in two cases compounding that with incidents in the race.

Russell never looked at team-mate Antonelli's level, compounding that with a lap-one track limits violation and, even though the penalty was perhaps harsh, that condemned him to finishing at the back of the top-four team group.

Lance Stroll's pace deficit to Alonso was similar to that of Russell versus Antonelli, which made the difference between his #18 Aston Martin being a backmarker rather than a midfield contender like the #14. Even the pitlane start was partly a result of the need to deal with damaged parts.

Much of Ollie Bearman’s weekend would make him a candidate for a high tier. Yet he didn't make the most of his pace in qualifying, as 13th-fastest turned to 16th when his final Q2 lap was deleted for a track limits violation, albeit one he strongly disputed. The early-race clash with Gasly at Turn 13 gave him damage that ruined his grand prix, with the stewards holding him responsible despite his protestations.

It was impossible to achieve anything in terms of results in a Williams, but Alex Albon had a so-so qualifying, lapping two tenths off Sainz. While his collision with Alonso at the hairpin on the first lap was by no means the torpedoing Alonso suggested it was, it was a high-risk move and gave Albon wing damage that compromised his race.

Franco Colapinto was put on the back foot through no fault of his own by a 10-place grid penalty, which means his qualifying deficit to Gasly wasn't a major factor in his placing - as he didn't focus on low-fuel pace work throughout the weekend. However, his pace overall never made an impact, and hitting Lindblad at Turn 1 was an error that ultimately put him out of the race.

There are three clear reasons. The first is the most important in that it is simply a more accurate way to compare the performances of drivers across a race weekend in terms of speed, consistency, racecraft, mistakes and the countless other criteria that relate to the driver's art.

Often, the feedback focuses on why there might be, for example, a five-place difference between two drivers who were at the same level but a tier list allows them to be ranked equally, while also maintaining their position relative to the rest of the field. By grouping the drivers, and having seven available tiers, it's a more meaningful way to differentiate between the performances of a group of drivers who are all operating at various levels of very good.

The second is that it is also easier for you to understand which drivers we consider to have done a better or worse job than others. By eliminating the need for infinitesimally small differentials, that should make it a more revealing exercise. Feedback has often focused on why, for example, two team-mates might be separated by four places in the middle of the rankings when there’s little or no meaningful difference between their performance. A tier list avoids this, and allows the focus to be on the more clear variations.

The third is that it's a more contemporary and visual way to present comparisons of athlete performance. The outstanding graphics that have been put together by our team demonstrate that far more effectively than any words could.
The same rigour and effort will still go into the rankings, but at The Race we believe this is a more up-to-date and representative way to digest the level of analysis we offer.
